headline: Hyundai's own self-driving software, Atria AI, will not be ready until 2029, about two years later than planned, and the group will use Nvidia's platform until then.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 by 2: Reuters and Quartz reported the 2029 timetable on 14 Sep 2026 (search listings), and this is a late secondary account with nothing clearly new.
importance_line: Hyundai buyers will not get the carmaker's own driving software before 2029, but this repeats September reporting, and Hyundai calls the plan acceleration while the media report a delay.
source: Motor Illustrated, citing Reuters and Korea JoongAng Daily
summary: Motor Illustrated reports, citing Reuters and the Korea JoongAng Daily, that Hyundai's in-house driver-assist software Atria AI is now due about two years later than planned, with the group relying on Nvidia's platform until then. Park Min-woo, described as a Nvidia veteran, is quoted by the JoongAng as saying he chose to slow down rather than rush a mediocre 'Level 2++' system (advanced driver assistance that still needs a supervising driver), while Hyundai's own press release spoke of acceleration.
notes: Search listings show Reuters and Quartz reporting the 2029 timetable on 14 Sep 2026, so this is old news re-dated; treat as a repeat in the final duplicate check.
